description: This line plot illustrates three accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—as functions of Initial Confidence, ranging from 0.81 to 0.99. The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale with tick marks spaced approximately every 0.01. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” also uses a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The “Final Accuracy” is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers, starting at approximately 1.00 and ending at approximately 0.99, showing minor fluctuations with a slight overall downward trend. The “Δ Accuracy” is shown as an orange dashed line with diamond markers, beginning at approximately 0.43 and ending at approximately 0.03, exhibiting a general downward trend with peaks around 0.43 and 0.30. The “Initial Accuracy” is depicted by a green dashed line with square markers, starting at approximately 0.55 and rising to approximately 0.98, showing a steady upward trend with minor fluctuations.
